products.name: Together AI
products.note: Decentralized cloud for open models; inference API; model hub; data residency options

reading.body:
Together AI operates a full-stack inference and compute platform for open-source models, positioning itself as infrastructure rather than a model developer, with emphasis on storage without egress fees and GPU scaling to support high-throughput workloads.

The company's $800 million in funding reflects a specific bet: that the economics of inference at scale favor open-source deployments over closed models. This is a buildings and power play dressed as software. Serverless inference APIs and managed GPU clusters are substitutes for the fixed capital that model providers must deploy. Together AI is betting it can aggregate demand across customers to achieve utilization rates that make that capital productive, while allowing users to retain data residency control.

For AI scaling, the constraint is not model quality but deployment cost. Egress fees are a known tax on inference at scale. Removing them addresses a real friction point, but the underlying constraint remains: GPU availability and power. Together AI's capability to scale to 30 billion tokens per model per inference depends on having those GPUs online and the power to run them. The platform itself adds no new compute or power. It redistributes existing capacity.

The data does not cover utilization rates, customer base, power consumption, or whether Together AI operates or merely coordinates its own infrastructure. It does not reveal whether the $800 million has been deployed and toward what capital expenses, or whether the research collaborations yield differentiating technology. It shows positioning and ambition, not outcome.

profile_text.body:
Together AI is a San Francisco company founded in 2022 that describes itself as an AI Native Cloud. According to its site, it offers a full-stack AI platform for inference, fine-tuning, and GPU clusters, and says it is powered by cutting-edge research. The site also describes asynchronous processing of large workloads, scaling to 30 billion tokens per model with any serverless model or private deployment, GPU infrastructure built for generative media workloads such as video, audio, and image models, and managed storage for AI workloads with object storage, parallel filesystems, and zero egress fees.

The company's tracked product is also named Together AI, listed under chat and general LLMs. Its note describes a decentralized cloud for open models, an inference API, a model hub, and data residency options. The site says Together Link brings frontier open models including GLM 5.3 and Kimi K3 into a team's existing coding agent and cuts model spend by over 50%. It also describes an open model AI stack of model, inference, gateways and routers, harness, and tools, where keeping each layer independent allows swapping in a new open model in minutes instead of rebuilding a workflow.

The site lists research contributors affiliated with Together AI alongside Carnegie Mellon University, Princeton University, Seoul National University, the University of California, Berkeley, Meta, NVIDIA, Colfax Research, Georgia Tech, and Cartesia A. No lawsuits or MCP servers are recorded for the company.
